content.title: Prelim Results | UFC Seattle
content.text: For the second straight year, the prelims in Seattle delivered plenty of excitement, with a collection of impressive finishes and a couple competitive battles that got the crowd at Climate Pledge Arena revved up and ready for the main card. In case you missed any of the action, catch up with our full fight recaps below. UFC Fight Night: Adesanya vs Pyfer took place Saturday, March 28, live from Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle, Washington. The prelims began at 5pm ET/2pm PT, followed by the main card at 8pm ET/5pm PT. The entire event can be relived on Paramount+. Watch Every UFC Event On Paramount+ Results, Highlights & Backstage Interviews Tofiq Musayev defeated Ignacio Bahamondes by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-27, 30-27) Tofiq Musayev earned a bloody win to close out Saturday’s prelims, battering Dana White’s Contender Series grad Ignacio Bahamondes with ground-and-pound that left him leaking, but it wasn’t without controversy. Bahamondes came out firing to start the second, hurting Musayev, who grabbed a handful of fence to avoid getting suplexed. From there, Musayev unloaded, busting up Bahamondes and leaving him covered in crimson at the end of the round. Tofiq Musayev of Azerbaijan reacts after the conclusion of a lightweight fight against Ignacio Bahamondes of Chile during the UFC Fight Night event at Climate Pledge Arena on March 28, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) In the third, Musayev put Bahamondes back on the canvas and continued to maul until the final minute of the round, where “La Jaula” briefly worked to the back before slipping off. This was a wildly entertaining fight, but in addition to the fence-grab, Musayev clearly headbutted Bahamondes in the second as well. There were absolutely tremendous moments from the native of Azerbaijan, however the fouls marred an otherwise captivating clash to wrap up the opening slate. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Lance Gibson Jr. defeated Chase Hooper by TKO (strikes) at 2:56 of Round 1 Lance Gibson Jr. registered his first UFC win in stunning fashion, starching Chase Hooper with a tight elbow in close that kicked off the finishing sequence. Lance Gibson Jr. Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle This was an emotional moment for “Fearless,” who was born in the Seattle and now earned his first UFC win in the city. He looked outstanding on Saturday after a solid showing in his short notice debut last December, and should continue to get more opportunities to shine after this one. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Tyrell Fortune defeated Marcin Tybura by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28) Newcomer Tyrell Fortune and veteran Marcin Tybura and continued the trend of heavyweight fights largely going the distance this year, with the two men engaging in a battle of attrition in Seattle on Saturday evening. Fortune wrestled well out of the gates, running Tybura to the ground with a powerful double leg and landing some damage while he had him on the canvas. Tyrell Fortune Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle But the Polish mainstay worked back standing, and from there, the duo primarily engaged on the feet, Fortune landing the better individual shots while Tybura throwing a little more volume and diversity. After back-to-back finishes, the judges were called upon to render a verdict, with all three seeing the fight in favor of Fortune. This was a good initial victory for the debuting heavyweight, who should climb into the rankings straight away and stand as another fresh name to track in the division going forward. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Casey O’Neill defeated Gabriella Fernandes by KO (strikes) at 3:11 of Round 1 Welcome back, “King” Casey O’Neill! Navajo Stirling Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle This was without question the best performance of Stirling’s young career and a sign of how much he continues to grow and develop between bouts. Just 28 years old, he remains one of the brightest emerging talents in the light heavyweight division, and kicked the night off for his team in impressive fashion. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Ricky Simon and Adrian Yanez fight to a majority draw (29-28, 28-28, 28-28) Ricky Simon and Adrian Yanez engaged in the kind of competitive back-and-forth battle everyone expected when it was announced, trading big shots for 15 minutes much to the delight of the crowd at Climate Pledge Arena. In all three rounds, the duo spent the majority of the frame exchanging at range, with Simon mixing in some grappling in the second to change up the tempo of the contest. Adrian Yanez punches Ricky Simon in a bantamweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Climate Pledge Arena on March 28, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Likely deadlocked at one round each heading into the final frame, the two men stood toe-to-toe and got after it, with Yanez unloading on Simon in the final seconds of the fight to seemingly salt things away. The judges were tasked with determining the victor and when the scores were totalled, the bout was scored a majority draw, with all three officials awarding Simon the first two rounds and two scoring the third 10-8 in favor of Yanez. This was an absolute slobberknocker and while the result didn’t land well with many, it doesn’t take away from how impressive each man looked on Saturday night. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Alexia Thainara defeated Bruna Brasil by unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-27) Alexia Thainara earned a measure of vengeance to open Saturday’s fight card in Seattle, bettering the only woman to have beaten her to date, Bruna Brasil, to advance to 3-0 in the UFC. The Season 8 Dana White’s Contender Series grad was the more active and diverse of the two throughout, landing at a much greater clip while mixing in timely takedowns to burn time off the clock. Alexia Thainara Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle Though she wasn’t able to find a finish, Thainara controlled the action throughout, even after eating a spinning back kick to the neck in the final minute of the fight. This was a strong result for Thainara, who took the fight on short notice and avenged the only loss of her career. The ranked 28-year-old has now won a dozen consecutive bouts overall and continued to position herself as an ascending person of interest in the strawweight ranks. | Main Card Results | Official Scorecards Still To Come:
